# Public pre-migration compatibility goldens

These fixtures contain public known-input encodings, extended public values and
an original public signature, never a customer key, private share, nonce, seed or
wrapping key. They are historical expectations, not regenerated by the candidate
under test.

`rustcrypto013-public-vectors.json` was generated with the unchanged pre-migration
Rust implementation, identical to main
`3d32b763ff777347f77eae7a8a7936d85dc2d770` (k256 0.13.4, elliptic-curve 0.13.8,
crypto-bigint 0.5.5). Inputs: byte lengths
0,1,2,31,32,33,63,64,65,127,128,129,257,1024, with byte `i` = `(73*i+19) mod 256`.
The test-only public HD root is generator multiplied by the publicly known integer
7, chain code `[0x91;32]`, paths m/0/{0,1,7,65535,2147483647}. This is no custody key
or signing fallback. The fingerprint domain is
`Custody/CRYPTO_BACKEND_PUBLIC_COMPAT_V1`; canonical public-vector fingerprint:
`c1ba561d0384ecbc1b7cc97ed17b99cfa521bd79cd63cf38b9bb15017da3d8a9`.

After the environment restart, the generator was recreated and matched the
persisted original output exactly before being run against the new backend. The
candidate's complete JSON matched that original output byte-for-byte. The test
now compares its current output to this committed historical fixture.

`rustcrypto013-signature.json` comes from a fresh genuine legacy 2-of-3 CGGMP
DKG/aux/root signing ceremony, independently verified with libsecp256k1. Only
original public execution/auxiliary request metadata, the public low-S signature
and its recovery metadata are retained. `high_s_signature` is the public
malleability counterpart `(r,n-s)`; candidate verification must reject it rather
than normalize-and-accept. The protocol test also rejects changed digests and
invalid encodings. The underlying private ceremony stores are excluded from Git.

The separate network CI gate rebuilds fixed original main and makes fresh private
fixtures for actual old-store loading, nonce fencing, receipt identity and all-pair
root/child/FROST signatures. Public goldens alone cannot prove private-store or
constant-time compatibility. Do not update these historical expectations merely
to make an incompatible candidate pass.
